read_file.rationale: Returns host-file data because it can `Read the complete contents of a file as text`; local file contents may be non-public. It is read-only and no advertised argument contacts an agent-chosen host.

read_text_file.rationale: Returns host-file data because it can `Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text` and `examine the contents of a single file`; allowed local file contents may be non-public. It is read-only and no advertised argument contacts an agent-chosen host.

read_media_file.rationale: Returns host-file data because it can `Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block`; local media or other file contents may be non-public. It is read-only and no advertised argument contacts an agent-chosen host.

read_multiple_files.rationale: Returns host-file data because it can `Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously` and `Each file's content is returned with its path as a reference`; local file contents and paths may be non-public. The returned path references are identifiers usable in later filesystem calls. It is read-only and no advertised argument contacts an agent-chosen host.

write_file.rationale: Changes local filesystem state because it can `Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content`; `path` selects the file written and `content` is stored. The description does not say it returns file contents or writes to an attacker-readable/public destination, only that it works `within allowed directories`.

edit_file.rationale: Changes and can reveal local file data because it can `Make line-based edits to a text file` and `Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made`; such a diff may include existing file lines from non-public local files. `path` selects the file changed, while `edits` carries replacement content. It does not advertise writing to an attacker-readable/public destination.

create_directory.rationale: Changes local filesystem state because it can `Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists`; `path` selects the directory created. The description does not say it returns non-public contents or sends data to an attacker-readable/public destination, only that it works `within allowed directories`.

list_directory.rationale: Returns non-public local filesystem structure because it can `Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path`; file and directory names are identifiers usable in later filesystem calls. It is read-only and no advertised argument contacts an agent-chosen host.

list_directory_with_sizes.rationale: Returns non-public local filesystem structure and metadata because it can `Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path, including sizes`; file and directory names are identifiers usable in later filesystem calls. It is read-only and no advertised argument contacts an agent-chosen host.

directory_tree.rationale: Returns non-public local filesystem structure because it can `Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure`; each entry includes `name`, which is an identifier usable in later filesystem calls. It is read-only and no advertised argument contacts an agent-chosen host.

move_file.rationale: Changes local filesystem state because it can `Move or rename files and directories`; `source` and `destination` decide which record is changed and where it moves. The description does not say it returns non-public contents or sends data to an attacker-readable/public destination, and says both paths must be `within allowed directories`.

search_files.rationale: Returns non-public local filesystem identifiers because it can `Recursively search for files and directories matching a pattern` and `Returns full paths to all matching items`; those full paths are identifiers usable in later filesystem calls. It is read-only and no advertised argument contacts an agent-chosen host.

get_file_info.rationale: Returns non-public local filesystem metadata because it can `Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory`, including `size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, and type`. It is read-only and no advertised argument contacts an agent-chosen host.

list_allowed_directories.rationale: Returns non-public host path information because it `Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access`; those directory paths are identifiers usable in later filesystem calls. It is read-only and has no destination argument.

notes: No tool is labeled UNTRUSTED because the threat model says the attacker does not control the user's local files, and the advertised filesystem tools only operate within local allowed directories.

No tool is labeled SINK because the advertised destinations are local filesystem paths, not attacker-chosen URLs, hosts, public repositories, public comments, or messages to attacker-readable recipients.
